MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MAY 21, 2025

  CHAIR STEGURA called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting of the
  City of Rolling Hills Estates at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Stegura, Bain, Chuang, McBurney, Rapoport, Rein

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Repp-Loadsman, Schmidt, Uppal

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Izabela Villalbazo, Office Assistant

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  MARCH 26, 2025.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MCBURNEY to,

  APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEEETING MINUTES OF
  MARCH 26, 2025.

  There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER REIN introduced himself to the committee. He stated that he is a retired
  engineer and has been living in the city since 1999.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS/ORAL COMMUNICATION ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE

  5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  Items taken out of order

  B.  CPA POWER READY PROGRAM

  Director Naughton introduced John Spector, Program Manager for Resilience and Grants and the
  Power Ready Program. Mr. Spector provided a presentation for the CPA Power Ready Program.
  He stated that the Power Ready Program helps local governments to meet climate adaptation
  strategies, overcome power outages, and aligns with climate action solutions. This program
  provides solar battery storage with power backup capabilities. Mr. Spector stated that they are a
  joint powers authority, and they are aggregating all the interested member sites in order to reduce
  the cost of the system. He further explained the Power Ready system. Mr. Spector explained the

ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  1
MEETING, MAY 21, 2025
   two pathways to participate in the program – member sites need to have an active CPA account
  and entities that will own the facility or in a 20-year long term lease. Some of the sites within the
  city that meet the criteria for critical service facilities are the churches, schools, hospitals, and
  specifically in the city – the PVP Library would be a good site. Technical assessments at interested
  sites are done for free and a proposal based on technical parameters and critical loads that the
  city would like backed up. If approved, CPA will host the public solicitation, as well as all monitoring
  of the system. Mr. Spector stated that there is no direct cost for participation, since for round one
  agencies are guaranteed that the total annual electric charges will be equal to or less than what
  would be paid without participating in the program.

  CHAIR STEGURA asked who pays for the battery storage unit. Mr. Spector stated that CPA pays
  for the unit.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN inquired about who the developers are and expressed concerns
  with issues that may arise with developers who go out of business. Mr. Spector stated that projects
  are put out to bid to various solar companies and CPA has step-in rights in their contracts with
  these companies. He also stated that CPA ranks developers on several criteria in order to minimize
  risk.

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS discussed potential sites within the city, including the PVP Library, fire
  station, schools, churches, and Peninsula Seniors.

  CHAIR STEGURA provided an explanation for the existing CPA program in the city.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER REIN suggested that staff ask for clarification from CPA, on any potential
  financial impacts to the City.

  CHAIR MADE A MOTION, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER RAPAPORT to,

  DIRECT STAFF TO ENGAGE WITH THE CPA TO IDENTIFY COMMUNITY PARTNERS
  THAT WOULD BENEFIT FROM THE POWER READY PROGRAM, DISCLOSE COSTS,
  AND REPORT BACK TO THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

  C. REQUEST TO RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL SUPPORT THE PROPOSED
  SOUTH COAST AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT DISTRICT RULES 1111 (REDUCTION OF
  NOx EMISSIONS FROM NATURAL GAS-FIRED FURNACES) AND 1121 (REDUCTION OF
  NOx EMISSIONS FROM RESIDENTIAL TYPE, NATURAL GAS-FIRED WATER HEATERS)

  Gary Tavetian, Sierra Club, stated that he retired from the California Attorney General’s Office in
  the Natural Resources Section and is now representing the Sierra Club. They are requesting that
  the City Council prepare a letter of support for the SCAQMD district rules 1111 and 1121. Mr.
  Tavetian stated that the SCAQMD will be voting on these rules on June 6 and emphasized that the
  board takes these letters of support into serious consideration. He provided a detailed explanation
  on how these rules work and how manufacturers of this equipment can comply. He further provided
  information on fees that manufacturers would need to pay to continue to sell gas-powered furnaces
  or water heaters. The SCAQMD is planning to put the fees into its “go-zero” fund in order to provide
  rebates to consumers who purchase electric powered heat pumps. Mr. Tavetian provided an
  overview of the cost to consumers to purchase electric powered heat pumps and savings in

ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  2
MEETING, MAY 21, 2025
   operating costs per year. He also explained the benefits in reduction of NOx emissions if there was
  full compliance in the South Bay per the assessment provided by the SCAQMD.

  A brief discussion ensued.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MCBURNEY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN
  to,
  RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL WRITE A LETTER IN SUPPORT OF SCAQMD
  DISTRICT RULES 1111 AND 1121.

  By majority vote, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

  D. SB 1383 - ORGANIC WASTE AND METHANE EMISSION REDUCTION – OVERVIEW

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided an overview on SB1383, which is one of the most
  significant waste reduction mandates to be adopted in CaliforniaSB1383 also looks to address
  climate change in that landfills release methane gas emissions.

  Assistant City Manager Davis stated that jurisdictions are required to make sure organic waste is
  collected, have an edible food recovery program, conduct outreach and education, and that the
  City has procured recycled and recovered edible products and established a procurement policy.
  In addition, the City will continue to look at food recovery capacity, and conduct ongoing monitoring
  of compliance and enforcement.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided an overview of the measures that the City has taken to
  implement SB1383, including:

  •  Establishing an ordinance in 2022
  •  Working on a food recovery program
  •  Education and outreach
  •  Establishing a procurement goal for recyclable or organic products
  •  Ongoing compliance and conducting enforcement

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MCBURNEY inquired if the City were to partner with PV Gardens to
  educate children about composting, would that help with education and outreach. Assistant City
  Manager Davis stated that this would be very helpful and stated that in the past they have
  participated in the City’s earth day celebration.

  Assistant City Manager stated that the green bin provided by Waste Management should be used
  to include any food waste. Additionally for commercial food generators, the City has provided
  information on food recovery organizations. Waste Management has a recycling hero program,
  where the haulers will nominate great recyclers and one person and one business will win a free
  year of waste services.

  Assistant City Manager stated that staff are working with a consultant to help identify gaps and to
  help move forward with initiatives. Additionally, the City does an annual compliance review with
  businesses, which may include site visits. The City is required to have detailed records to
  CalRecycle within 10 business days of receiving a request; to help with this, the City works with
  City Green to meet the compliance requirements.

ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  3
MEETING, MAY 21, 2025
   The City received grant money from CalRecycle that helped fund the services provided by City
  Connect, the database that staff is using, and will also help to extend the subscription as well as
  any other need for consultants.

  A.  PLASTIC POLLUTION PREVENTION

  Director Naughton stated that staff has reached out to the PVP Chamber of Commerce, and they
  are on board with the City providing a survey to the businesses regarding recyclable/compostable
  cutlery and to gauge the level of support of a recognition and promotion program within the
  community. She provided a QR code, which brings up a draft of the survey questionnaire.

  Director Naughton stated that staff connected with Martha Segovia at the SBCCOG and confirmed
  that they have received the green business tracker tool provided for the South Bay cities and have
  begun working on implementation. Staff are meeting with the SBCCOG to help them understand
  the needs of the City and staff will return with an update.

  Director Naughton stated that Committee Member Uppal provided an update from the Chair of
  PVPUSD’s Sustainability Committee, and they reported that all ten schools have
  compostable/recyclable trays; however, they are still using plastic service ware and small plastic
  serving cups, and high schools are using paper and plastic service bowls and plastic service ware.
  They stated that one of the challenges is that the food is prepped at a central kitchen and
  paper/compostable containers will not work for shipping to the schools, and waste hauling services
  vary in the different cities on the Peninsula.

  6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  8.  ADJOURNMENT
